text:
Maya Patel: Hey all — Support is getting a bunch of “what’s the ETA for our Dedicated GPU expansion to be ready?” questions again.

We have older canned language that basically says “2–5 business days” which is… not great and also not aligned w/ the new readiness gates.

Can someone give me updated ETA / wording that’s safe to send to customers? Also: how should we describe “ready” vs “provisioned” so we don’t accidentally imply they’re live in routing.

Related ticket: SUP-2201 (delayed expansion). Also have an external email thread w/ customer asking for a firm time window.

Refs:
- Confluence overview: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENGINFRA/Provision-to-ready+automation+overview
- Gmail thread (Vanessa): https://mail.google.com/mail/u/0/#search/rfc822msgid%3A<thread-4f12aa90ce@redwood>

Vanessa Ortiz: Yup, thanks for flagging. The short version is:
- We can’t promise an exact time until capacity is allocated (region/SKU constraints still apply).
- Once the infra run actually starts, we *can* give tighter updates based on stage progress.

For language, I’d separate:
1) lead time to *start* (depends on GPU availability / maintenance window)
2) time-to-ready once started (automation pipeline)

Current pilot goal for time-to-ready (once started) is “same day” in most cases. Internally we’re seeing p50 ~4h and p95 ~8–10h when there’s no quota/IAM drama.

Important: “ready” means the pool passed validation + perf-canary and is eligible for routing. “provisioned” just means infra exists.

Lauren Bishop: +1 on splitting those. For customer-facing wording, I’d avoid quoting p50/p95 numbers as hard commitments unless we have a contract SLO.

Suggested safe copy (feel free to paste into macros):

“Dedicated capacity expansions have two parts: (1) scheduling/allocating GPUs in your requested region/SKU and (2) bringing the capacity online through our provisioning + validation pipeline. Once provisioning starts, we run automated networking, GPU health, and runtime readiness checks and only mark the pool ‘Ready’ after it passes validation. We’ll share progress updates as each stage completes, and we’ll confirm when the new capacity is Ready (i.e., eligible for routing).”

If customer is pushing for a window, we can say “we typically complete provisioning + validation within the same business day once started” but make it clear it’s “typical” not a guarantee.

Rafael Mendes: From SRE POV: please don’t say “it’s live” until control plane state is Ready. During Validating we keep it out of routing on purpose (we had that intermittent 5xx during validation window last week).

Also worth adding a sentence like “If any check fails, we automatically stop and remediate before enabling routing” — sets expectation that delays are safety-related, not random.

Harish Reddy: For the SUP-2201 style situations, the most helpful thing for Support is giving customers *stage-based* updates (not just “still working on it”).

Something like:
- “Provisioning started”
- “Imaging in progress”
- “Bootstrapping cluster”
- “Running validation checks”
- “Ready (handed to routing)”

We can also give an ETA once we’re past imaging (that’s where we’ve seen most variance by region).

Kira Thompson: If you want an “approved” definition snippet, here’s the wording we’re using in runbooks (feel free to lift a simplified version):

- Provisioned: infrastructure created + nodes present, but not yet validated; not eligible for routing.
- Ready: all readiness gates passed (network/DNS/TLS, GPU health, runtime smoke test, perf-canary), control plane state set to Ready; eligible for routing.

Also linking the runbook section that explains common delays (quota, artifact mirror, GPU ECC): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENGINFRA/Dedicated+pool+provisioning+runbook#Customer-comms

Maya Patel: This is perfect. I’ll update our macro to:
- split “allocation/scheduling” vs “provisioning+validation”
- define Ready explicitly as “eligible for routing”
- promise stage-based updates once provisioning starts

For the customer thread, I’ll use “same business day once started” as “typical” and caveat region/SKU constraints.

If anyone has a stronger “do/don’t say” list, drop it here.

Vanessa Ortiz: Do say:
- “eligible for routing” when Ready
- “validation gates” / “safety checks”
- “we’ll post stage updates”

Don’t say:
- exact hours as a guarantee
- “ready = installed” / “ready = provisioned”

(reactions: :thumbsup: x4)

Lauren Bishop: Works. If Sales/CS asks for a single line: “Once GPUs are allocated, we bring the pool online via an automated provision-to-ready pipeline and confirm when it’s Ready (validated + eligible for routing).”

Rafael Mendes: +1. Also, if a customer asks why we can’t cut corners: “we intentionally keep new capacity out of routing until validation completes to avoid intermittent errors.” That’s the honest answer.

Maya Patel: Got it. Updating now + will reply to SUP-2201 with stage-based language. Thanks all.
